title: Process simplification and cost: affected-test gates, converging reviews, honest prices
description: Merges the handoff's phase 2 (process simplification, sketch section 0) and phase 4 (cost: F597 and F577 first, then research N1-N5, then sketch section 3 incl. 3a) into one phase so it is reviewed once. Order inside the phase follows the handoff: the meter's dedup (F597) lands before any task that produces or prints a cost figure, because every figure after it would otherwise be biased in the plugin's favour; the price table (F577/N1) lands before Haiku-first review (N2) and the CI cost gate, because Haiku 5.5 is priced at `_default` today. Process items: affected-test gates per task with the full gate once per phase (F596, incl. its e2e extension), derived follower scope, review convergence (F605), one-command release. Cost items: one price table with effective dates and record-time stamping (3a), the CLI's costUSD beside the plugin's reading, the reviewer's diff computed once (N5), Haiku-first review behind a config key (N2), the git-snapshot report (N4), maxTurns caps (N12), cache-friendly dispatch prompts and briefs, an enforced one-line hand-back (F567), a CI cost regression gate over recorded sessions, and a design-and-measurement task only for running the phase cycle as a plugin Workflow (N3, implementation needs a paid probe). F575 is not included: it was addressed by P119.7 and P121.12. Prices were verified against Anthropic's pricing and models pages on 2026-10-10 (quoted in openChoices). No task makes a paid model call. Open choices settled by the orchestrator under the user's overnight mandate (2026-10-10), each the structurally correct option: one price table living in hooks/_config.py with _usage_core deriving it; no shipped _default row (a project-declared one is still honoured); effectiveFrom = the date the plugin first read the rate, older rows labelled; ship the published rate and show the CLI reading beside it, calling neither the bill; a carried low goes to a pending task in one plan-level carry-forward phase; Haiku-first review off by default behind review.cascade; e2e selection = runner related list + changed list + meta.coupling, else every spec with the reason printed; followers for user projects from meta.followers.command plus F599 companions; hand-backs enforced by a SubagentStop hook after a payload probe; the CI cost gate reads redacted committed recordings; maxTurns = 2x the largest measured request count with the command beside it; F575 closed in the register after one timed run.
desiredOutcome: A task gate runs what the change can break, sign-off converges in at most the configured rounds, and every cost figure is priced at the rate in effect when it was recorded.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/report/_report_usage.py, plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_usage.py:189 (P125.3, untouched; both declared in the task's files)
findings.issue: P125.3 clause 'every surface (audit-usage, the report, the panel) prints unpriced beside its tokens instead of a dollar figure' is contradicted. Only audit-usage.py gained `cost_cell` and the 'tokens unpriced' text. The panel still sums `float(r.get('costUSD') or 0.0)`, and neither file mentions 'unpriced' or `unpricedTokens` at HEAD. An unpriced model's spend therefore reads as free in the report and the panel. The executor's claim defers these to P125.4, whose diff did not touch them either.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.75-0h5 (ce9b2c34be03): Carry `unpricedTokens` (already summed by `_usage_core.totals`/`_finish`) into the report payload (`window.AUDIT_USAGE`) and the panel facts. Render 'unpriced' beside the tokens of a model that has no price, and state how many tokens a cost total leaves out. Add cases in test__report_usage.py and test__panel_usage.py.

findings.issue: P125.3 clause 'returns the count of each so every surface's rate phrase states the mix' is contradicted. `priced_at_read` returns only `pricedWhenWritten`, and that is now the count of unstamped, unpriceable rows only. The stamped and unstamped counts are not returned. The rate phrase still reads as 'costs priced at <resolved table>', although stamped rows are priced from their own stamp and are no longer touched by the table it names. That is a printed claim with no basis.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.75-0h5 (ce9b2c34be03): Return `stamped` and `readPriced` (and `kept`) counts from `priced_at_read`. Have `rate_basis_phrase` say 'N rows at the rate stamped when written, M priced again at the rate in effect on their date'. Add a case pinning the phrase with a mixed ledger.

findings.issue: P125.3 clause 'rows are priced at global routing and the basis says so' is not implemented. No text under plugins/audit says 'global' or 'inference-geo' (grep at HEAD), and the diff changes neither the basis phrase nor the README in that respect.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.75-0h5 (ce9b2c34be03): Add the routing statement to the printed rate basis and to the README usage section ('priced at global routing; inference-geo pricing is not visible in the transcript'). Pin it with a case.

findings.issue: P125.4 clause 'The meter records the CLI's per-model figure per session beside the plugin's own reading' is contradicted. Nothing is recorded: the hook and the ledger writer are untouched, and `read_cost_state` is called at dashboard time. The clause 'audit-usage, the report and the panel print both wherever they differ' is also contradicted: report and panel have no `cli_cost` path at HEAD. A later commit (a7d1b5c4, P125.39) added a once-per-session note, which does not supply either.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.76-0h5 (3ecc6df213e1): Either record the per-session CLI figure at meter time (a field on the cursor or a ledger row) and have the report and panel read it, or amend the task text to the render-time design and file the report/panel surfaces as an explicit follow-up task.

findings.issue: The probe clause asked for modelUsage compared to the ledger's per-model sum for that session. The docstring answers 'modelUsage DOES fold in subagent spend' from the absence of sonnet in the main transcript. It then admits the two sides disagree 'by a wide margin, on every model' and attributes this to compaction, which is unverified. The stated answer is an inference, not a measured comparison.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.76-0h5 (3ecc6df213e1): Re-run the probe as asked: per model, `modelUsage` costUSD against the ledger's per-model sum for that session id, with and without subagent rows. Record the numbers in the docstring, or reword the docstring to 'inferred, not measured'.

findings.issue: The doctor's remedy is 'add a usage.pricing row'. After P125.3 a row stamped `rate: None` stays unpriced forever, because `priced_at_read` never re-resolves a stamped row (rs2). Only `--backfill` rewrites it. `check_unpriced_models` asks `rates_for(model, pricing)`, not the rows' own `unpriced` flag, so after the row is added the doctor goes green while every dollar total still leaves those tokens out.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.77-0h5 (4bc5e5f9f097): Make the check count rows that carry `unpriced: True` or `rate: None`, and have the remedy name `/audit:usage --backfill` as the second step. Or let `priced_at_read` re-resolve a row whose stamp is None.

findings.issue: P125.2 clause (1) names `_loader.load_hooks_config()` as the route. The diff adds a raw `importlib` loader (`_load_hooks_config_module`), another hand-rolled loader copy, with a comment arguing layering. The clause is not followed and the task's own openChoices alternative is not recorded as taken.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.77-0h5 (4bc5e5f9f097): Either route through `_loader` (moving `_usage_core`'s layer if needed) or record the layering decision in the manifest and the task text so the clause matches the code.

findings.issue: The declared case 'DEFAULT_PRICING is the hooks/_config table read through _loader, not a second literal (an edit to hooks/_config alone changes it)' cannot fail on the mutation it names. dp4 loads an edited scratch copy with `_loader.load` and checks that module, so it never touches `_usage_core.DEFAULT_PRICING`. dp1 only checks that `M._hooks_config` exists, and dp2 compares equal content, which a hand-copied literal that kept `_hooks_config` would also satisfy. The comment in hooks/_config.py says 'the `dp` case asserts an edit here alone moves the copy', which dp does not.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.77-0h5 (4bc5e5f9f097): Make dp4 load a scratch hooks/_config.py through the same function `_usage_core` uses at import (or reload `_usage_core` against it) and assert `DEFAULT_PRICING` moved. Or correct the hooks/_config.py comment.

findings.issue: P125.2 clause (4) says a project-declared `_default` is 'still honoured and labelled'. Honoured, yes. Nothing labels a row or cost priced through a declared `_default`; it prints like any priced row.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.77-0h5 (4bc5e5f9f097): Have `rate_for_stamp` / the rate basis note when the answering entry was `_default` (for example `rateVia: '_default'` on the stamp and a phrase on the surfaces), or amend the task.

findings.issue: P125.2 removed the shipped `_default`, so `price()` returns None for an unknown model while the write path still did `round(price(...), 6)`. At that commit an unknown model raised TypeError in the meter. Fixed at HEAD by 372ab613 (P125.3), which sets `costUSD` None and `unpriced` True.
findings.resolution: Fixed at HEAD by 372ab613. Nothing further.

findings.issue: The Haiku 5.5 long-prompt row, required by P125.2 clause (2), was not added to the shipped table. P125.3 added it afterwards as `LONG_PROMPT_RATES` in `_usage_core`, outside the hooks/_config.py table, which splits the shipped prices across two homes.
findings.resolution: Fixed at HEAD by 372ab613 (P125.3), in a different place from the one the P125.2 clause named. Record the split in the task text, or fold the row into the single table.

findings.issue: The filed return has outcome.technical and outcome.descriptive set to 'placeholder' and testsAdded set to [], while the diff added many cases (dp, dr, pr6-8, cc5/6/6b, sc0*). The claim does not describe the diff.
findings.resolution: Re-file with the outcome text and tests list. Nothing else in the code changes.

findings.issue: 'both equal the checked-in page excerpt' is checked by comparing the table to hard-coded literals in the test and, separately, checking that the fixture contains the same hand-typed strings. The excerpt is never parsed against the table, so the table and the fixture can drift together unnoticed. One substring check is a no-op ('not in').
findings.resolution: Parse the fixture's table rows and compare them field by field with `rates_for`. Drop the no-op substring check.

findings.issue: up1 asserts the model id and the word 'unpriced' appear anywhere in the --by render. It cannot tell the `cost_cell` output from any other occurrence of the word, such as the notice in the total line, so it does not prove the cell prints 'unpriced' for that row.
findings.resolution: Assert on the model's own table row (the line containing 'claude-future-9' carries 'unpriced' and no '$').

findings.issue: The ledger row's `model` is now the synthetic id 'claude-haiku-5-5:long-prompt', so every by-model rollup, the routing advice and the doctor see a model that does not exist. P125.4 needs an `_base_model` strip to compare it. If such a row is priced against a table that lacks the tiered row, `rates_for` falls through to the longest prefix and silently prices it at the base rate. All current callers go through `resolve_pricing`, so this is a latent risk, not an active one.
findings.resolution: Keep `model` as the real id and carry the tier as a separate row field or group-key part. Group and price on (model, tier). Drop `_base_model`.

findings.issue: `cli_cost_lines` compares the CLI's cumulative per-session `cost-state` with `rows`, which are only the rows in the --since/--until window. A windowed view reports a false 'differ' with both figures. `main` also reads each in-view transcript in full on every dashboard run.
findings.resolution: Compare against all of the session's ledger rows (or print the section only for an all-time window). Cache or bound the transcript read.

findings.issue: `ul = _trail._load('usage_ledger', ...)` was moved out of the `try` that guarded it (it ran only under `if transcript_path`), and `check_unpriced_models` calls `_load` unguarded. A load failure now crashes doctor, which is documented as read-only and diagnostic, instead of degrading to `pricing = None`.
findings.resolution: Wrap both `_load` calls in the existing try/except and report a warn.

findings.issue: The check counted non-model ids (the `<synthetic>` placeholder) as unpriced models. Fixed at HEAD by 8f5d7255 (P125.52), which makes the check ignore ids that are not models. | The shipped unpriced check fired on '<synthetic>' ids (2 of 31 recorded sessions in the executor's own measurement, a false positive). Fixed at HEAD by 8f5d7255 (P125.52, is_model_id guard).
findings.resolution: Fixed at HEAD by 8f5d7255; no action.

findings.issue: The `rev-parse --verify` subprocess call sits outside the `try`, so an OSError or TimeoutExpired there raises out of `compose_phase_brief` instead of producing the 'run it yourself' fallback. Diffs are also embedded for every listed task, not only owed ones, which grows the brief. A path list built from `files` with a directory entry would show every file under it as 'outside every task's declared files'.
findings.resolution: Move the rev-parse call inside the try/except. Restrict `shown` to owed tasks, or document that all listed tasks are shown. Match directory entries by prefix when computing 'outside'.

findings.issue: The task asked for 'a main-transcript fixture whose repeats are identical records exactly one message' and for the existing streaming-partial cases to 'stay green'. The diff adds no new identical-repeat fixture, and it rewrites sf4's assertion (from `not pend` to a non-empty tally) to match the new behaviour. sf8, the lower-counts case, would also pass on the old code.
findings.resolution: Add an identical-repeats case (3 identical entries record 1 msg and no extra row). Note the sf4 assertion change in the filed return.

findings.issue: verify-release (sh tools/verify.sh --release) runs BEFORE the release commit. verify.sh --release ends with 'HEAD carries the published pages' (check-rendered-artifacts.py --against-commit), and tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py / CONTRIBUTING.md state that this arm is red for as long as a re-rendered page is uncommitted. The bump and followers steps always re-render version-stamped pages, so on a real run verify-release cannot pass and the pipeline stops there every time. The selftest's FakeRunner returns (0, '') for the verify.sh call, so the order is never exercised.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.74-0h5 (73b282eb86e4): Run commit before verify-release (or run the --before-commit half before the commit and the full --release after it), and add a case whose fake verify.sh answer depends on whether a commit was recorded.

findings.issue: wait_ci resolves the pushed branch with `git rev-parse ci/v<version>`, but step_push_ci_branch pushes `HEAD:refs/heads/ci/v<version>` and creates no local branch; only refs/remotes/origin/ci/v<version> exists. Checked in a scratch repo: after that push `git rev-parse ci/v1.2.3` exits 128 ('unknown revision') while `git rev-parse origin/ci/v1.2.3` resolves. So with --push the wait-ci step always stops 'could not resolve ci/v... to a commit'. rl3/rl4/rl5 stub `git rev-parse ci/v9.9.9` to succeed, so no case can fail on this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.74-0h5 (73b282eb86e4): Resolve the SHA from HEAD at push time (store it in state with ciBranch) or use `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`/`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>`, and make the fake runner answer rev-parse of a bare ci/ ref with failure.

findings.issue: A run without --push records push-ci-branch, wait-ci, push-main-tag, gh-release and check-published as status 'done' ('skipped: no --push given'), and run_pipeline skips any step already done. A later `release.py run --version X --push` therefore finds every remote step done, publishes nothing and prints 'RELEASE vX COMPLETE'; the local tag step has already run too. rl2b asserts exactly this recording as intended. The documented dry-run-then-push use ends in a false success.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.74-0h5 (73b282eb86e4): Record a skipped remote step as 'skipped' (not 'done') and treat it as pending when --push is given, or refuse a --push resume over a state file whose remote steps were skipped; add a case that runs without --push and then with it and expects the push.

findings.issue: Task clause 'guard-release learns to treat an invocation of tools/release.py as a publishing command so the #release-with-bugs bypass still governs it' is not implemented: the hook has no hunk and the declared test 'python3 tools/release.py --push is classified as a publishing command' was not written. The open-bug rule exists only inside release.py (release_permitted), so the hook never sees the release command.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.104-0h5 (3299d01909c6): Add the release.py arm to the guard's publisher classification with a case in the hook's suite, or have the owner amend the task description and its tests.add so the override is recorded where the gate reads it.

findings.issue: Clause 'including resume after a stop at each step' is met only for the CI step (rl3/rl4). No case stops at bump, changelog, followers, verify-release, commit, push, tag, push-main-tag or gh-release and resumes, which is how findings 1 to 3 survived a green selftest.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.74-0h5 (73b282eb86e4): Drive a table of steps, failing each in turn with the fake runner and resuming, asserting the earlier steps do not re-run and the failed one does.

findings.issue: The bypass slot is looked up with os.environ CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, while arm-release-bypass.py names the slot from the hook payload's session_id, and with no id both sides use 'release-bypass-none.json'. Nothing shown establishes that the env value equals the payload value, and rl11's 'no session id, no bypass possible' is false if a 'none' slot file exists.
findings.resolution: Read the session id the way the hook receives it (or refuse a bypass when the env id is absent), and say in the docstring what that variable is verified to be.

findings.issue: The clause 'record them as this plan's related/all listing' is not done in this diff, so the listing modes were unused and every P125 task gate stayed the full phase gate. Fixed at HEAD by 9f1251db: the plan now records listing.all, listing.related and spelling.
findings.resolution: Fixed at HEAD by 9f1251db; no action.

findings.issue: --list-all prints only test* files under plugins/audit/tests, while tools/sweep-selftests.py SWEEP_DIRS also collects hooks, scripts, tools and .claude/hooks; --list-related prints select()'s suites only and discards its gates (browser, vitest, parity). A listing that says 'the full suite' while omitting what the runner collects can make derive-phase-gate read a narrowed answer as equal to the wide one.
findings.resolution: Either list every file the sweep collects (reuse SWEEP_DIRS) or state in the docstring and CONTRIBUTING.md that the listing is the tests/ tree and the other gates stay in the task's own gate.

findings.issue: The related listing is checked against the recorded verifiedOn version answer; the e2eChanged listing (a different runner) is trusted with no version check, so a stale e2e listing is read as current.
findings.resolution: Verify the e2e listing against its own recorded version, or document that only `related` is version-verified.

findings.issue: The diff restated _gate_derive's two version checks and read meta.coupling. Fixed at HEAD: P125.49 (0e549bc4) routes the check through _gate_derive.version_distrust, and P125.45 (354c968e) removed the coupling arm.
findings.resolution: Fixed at HEAD by 0e549bc4 and 354c968e; no action.

findings.issue: The headline case 'one med and two lows: one fix, two reviews, signed off' asserts only fix count, review count, DONE and signed, which also hold on the pre-change driver (lows signed off open, no carry). It is not red-capable; the carried assertions are in cv2. The executor's own failing list at HEAD omits cv1 and lf2.
findings.resolution: Move the status == 'carried' / carriedTo assertion into cv1 so the named case fails on the old driver.

findings.issue: dispatch_starts orders dispatches by file mtime and its docstring says that is 'the order a session actually spawned them in'. An mtime is the time of the last write, i.e. roughly when a dispatch finished, so a long first dispatch that ends after a second one starts swaps them. check_dispatch_cache then prints 'dispatch X read N cached token(s) at its start, served from <prev>'s' (lines 268-273), naming a predecessor as the cache's source on that ordering alone. The output asserts a cause that nothing in the reading establishes. Still true at HEAD (_doctor_trail.py:466-482).
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.83-0h5 (7539f5577ec0): Order by the first entry's timestamp inside each transcript (the first usage block is already read), or drop the 'served from <prev>' attribution and print only the read/written tokens; correct the docstring either way.

findings.issue: Task says each later dispatch's first-request cache 'read and write' is shown. The branch prints only the read when cacheRead > 0 (a dispatch that read 3000 and wrote 500 shows no write) and, when both are zero, prints 'was NOT served from ... it wrote 0 token(s)'. Also an unparseable settings file is dropped (`_broken` unused in check_git_instructions, _doctor_setup.py:150), so a broken project settings.json reads 'on (default)'.
findings.resolution: Print both counts in every branch, say 'no cache activity' when both are zero, and name an unreadable settings file in the git-instructions row.

findings.issue: The task clause 'the command body (commands/phase.md and the run/drive reference) directs a fresh context per phase ... stated as the step, not a tip' contradicts task clause: phase.md is not edited by the diff and still has no clear-context text at HEAD. The direction exists only as a drive STEPS line (drive-phase.py:374-385) and orchestrator.md prose, which the executor chose because phase.md sat at its measured byte ceiling.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.84-0h5 (6cb3e5fd58d1): Add the one-sentence directive to commands/phase.md (making room by trimming another line under measure-context.py's ceiling), or have the plan owner amend the clause to say the drive print is the step.

findings.issue: The task's micro-test (two trivial phases driven back to back as the command directs; the second phase's first orchestrator request carries no more context than a fresh entry within a stated margin, offline fixture over recorded transcript rows) contradicts task clause: it is absent. cn1/cn2 only check that finish() prints a chain line; no margin is stated or measured.
findings.resolution: Add the offline fixture over recorded transcript rows with a named margin, or record the omission on the task.

findings.issue: Task says the drive's entry line reads the context size; drive-phase.py prints no such line (only audit-status --short, echoed by next/run/resume, and the full render do), and the filed claim says render_short is 'the entry view the step driver's loop echoes'. Also the line prints `each further request costs ~$X` from a fresh-`in` (no-cache) upper bound, and the threshold is not stated in the line, so the figure carries neither its basis nor 'upper bound'.
findings.resolution: Name the surface in the claim/docs accurately or add the line to the drive's entry; print 'at most ~$X, uncached' and the threshold (usage_ledger.LONG_PROMPT_THRESHOLD_TOKENS) beside it.

findings.issue: The task's clause (8) that a contradicted clause carries a MED floor contradicts task clause in effect: CLAUSE_QUOTING_LINES tells the reviewer a finding 'names a contradicted task clause' is floored, but floor_contradicted_clause matches only the literal substring 'contradicts task clause' (_CONTRADICTED_CLAUSE_MARKER). The brief's wording does not contain it, so a low finding saying 'contradicted' or 'diverges from the clause' is not raised. Still true at HEAD.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.86-0h5 (083c9f45fd01): State the exact marker in CLAUSE_QUOTING_LINES ('start the issue with "contradicts task clause"'), or match several spellings, and add a case on the brief text.

findings.issue: Task clause (5) says every planned test carries a 'must fail if' line and the drive applies it in a temp tree after the executor files; the diff wires nothing (run_falsifier stays unreferenced by the pipeline) and rewrites phase-signoff.md to 'A planned test MAY carry a falsifier ... nothing in the pipeline calls it automatically', contradicts task clause (5). The executor documents why (no schema field in its files). | Orchestrator item 7: recorded as carried to P128 by an earlier decision. At 8e7c5121 run_falsifier (drive-phase.py:1300) still has no caller, and docs/audit/phases/P128.json names no falsifier or 'must fail if' task, so the carry is not on the plan.
findings.resolution: Open a follow-up task owning schema/_manifest_rules plus the wiring, or amend clause (5) on the plan; do not leave the delivered text as the answer to the clause.

findings.issue: This commit rewrites compose_reviewer_brief and compose_phase_brief (clause-quoting section, tests.add lines, claim-last order) and the declared tests.add names the brief cases, but no case in the diff pins them (test_audit_lookup.py, test_drive_phase.py and test__filed_returns.py are unchanged here and at HEAD no case asserts CLAUSE_QUOTING_LINES, _tests_add_review_lines or the ordering). Deleting those lines leaves the swept suites green.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.79-0h5 (f6403a168ad7): Add cases asserting both briefs contain the clause rule and tests.add, and that '## Task' then '## Claim under review' are the last section.

findings.issue: Clause (9) says a declared case may match 'by a clause mapping the return files'; tests_add_gaps reads `tests.addMap` from the task, not a mapping in the filed return.
findings.resolution: Accept an `addMap` in the return, or reword the clause.

findings.issue: _INTERACTION_PSEUDO_RE requires :focus/:hover to be followed by whitespace, ',', '{' or ':', so `.field input:focus-visible` and `:focus-within` yield no parity entry (checked against the regex), and a commented-out rule is matched. Every .css in `files` is treated as a design source, and the synthesized tests.add entry names the .css itself as the 'test file' path.
findings.resolution: Include focus-visible/focus-within, strip comments before matching, and name the control's test location rather than the stylesheet.

findings.issue: The task rule is 'a task that adds or changes observable behaviour is tdd', but the new default is a keyword scan of title plus description checked refactor first, then config, else tdd. _CONFIG_TEXT now also matches 'document(s|ing|ation)' besides comment(s)/docs/config, so 'Add comments to posts' or 'Let users upload a document' is written gate-only with no red-first, and 'extract the CSV' text is written regression. This makes the misclassification the silent default for every `add` and batch task.
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.87-0h5 (dbbbb2fd93ff): Classify on the title only or require the signal word to head the title, and name the matched word in the note so a wrong arm is visible; add a case for a feature whose text contains 'comment' or 'document'.

findings.issue: The _batch_doc fixture was given an explicit tests.mode to avoid a timestamped note making two writes (file vs stdin) differ, so the new default's volatile `_utc_now()` note is hidden rather than covered; the filed claim also lists execute-task.md/audit-executor.md edits this commit does not contain.
findings.resolution: Cover the classified-note path in the fb13 byte-identity case with a fixed clock, and correct the claim.

findings.issue: Task names the 'is not exported' error; only the node ESM wording 'does not provide an export named' is read, the row is limited to runners vitest/jest/None (a playwright run is excluded), and se1/se2 exercise only that wording. A rollup/vite `"x" is not exported by "y"` error is still not an --introduces proof. Still true at HEAD (stamp-verification.py:687).
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.80-0h5 (dbd9008f4458): Add the 'is not exported by' spelling (named group for the export) to the row and a case for it, or state the wording the testbed actually printed.

findings.issue: playwright_line_cases marks every entry `assertion: True` ('playwright: failed'), so a line-reporter run failing on a timeout, a refused connection or a crash proves red as 'a task's own case failing an assertion'. The docstring admits it; the weakening is in the proof the red word rests on. Still true at HEAD (_runner_output.py:698).
findings.resolution: fixed in P125.80-0h5 (dbd9008f4458): Mark line-reporter entries `assertion: None/unknown` and let red say it proved a failure, not an assertion, or require the JSON reporter for `proved`.

findings.issue: scs1 asserts behaviour that pre-dates the task (a run with `problem` set is could-not-prove) and passed on unfixed code, as did se2; the filed claim says all 7 cases were 'run red against the pre-fix code'. tasks.title: Sign-off converges: re-review only for med+ or red fixes, lows carried, rounds capped
tasks.description: F605. In drive-phase's triage: (1) a re-review is owed only for a fix task whose finding was med or high, or whose gate went red; a fixed low closes on its own green gate and fixes_after()/owed_tasks() stop listing it. (2) The triage's recommended answer for a low finding is carry (status `carried`, carriedTo a parked task - see openChoices for the target), and render_triage prints that as the default; fix stays available. (3) A re-review reads only the fix tasks' diffs (phase-diff-in-brief) and its brief says a new low in a fix is carried, not looped. (4) A round cap per phase, config review.maxRounds (default 2): reaching it prints the findings still open, the rounds' cost so far read from the usage ledger by phase (with its pricing basis, or 'unpriced' where it is), and asks once (carry all / one more round / sign-off with accept-open). The cap and the counts live in the driver's state, so a lost state file re-derives the round count from the filed phase returns rather than resetting to zero. Add the config key to hooks/_config.py DEFAULTS, _config_rules, the schema and the README config table. Red first: a review returning one med and two lows dispatches one fix task and one re-review over that fix's diff, the two lows end carried, and no third review is dispatched. Also measured in P123's review rounds: a fix task made from a finding defaults to tdd even when the finding is a missing test or a pin over a fix that already landed (P123.63, P123.66), so the red-first helper rightly refuses it and the task must be cancelled and re-added as regression - choose the fix task's mode from the finding: a finding whose resolution only adds a case over code already at HEAD is regression, with the red shown by restoring the old code in a scratch copy.

tasks.title: A task gate also runs every test its change can break; the full gate runs once per phase
tasks.description: F596 incl. its EXTENSION. New pure module _affected_tests: given the task's changed paths (from its diff against the phase head in the task's own tree; a rename counts as both its old and new path, a deletion as its old path) and the project's observations, return the suites to add to the task's gate and the basis for each. Arms, in order: the project's related listing (meta.phaseGate.derived.listing.related, the same recorded and version-verified listing derive-phase-gate already trusts, e.g. vitest related / jest --findRelatedTests --listTests); for Python, a stdlib ast import graph from test files to the changed modules; the e2e runner's changed listing when one is recorded; meta.coupling entries whose sources overlap; and the e2e widening rule in openChoices. A listing that cannot run is a printed skip reason and widens to the phase gate, never an empty selection read as 'nothing affected'. run-test-gate.py, when it measures a task, runs the union of the task's own gate and the affected set and records which suites came from which arm in the evidence row. The phase's sign-off gate stays the wide one (derived narrowing remains the opt-in meta.phaseGate.mode it is today), so the full gate runs once per phase. Regression case from the testbed: a task that moves app/page.tsx to app/[locale]/page.tsx selects the smoke test that imports @/app/page, and its gate goes red.

tasks.title: tools/release.py cuts a release end to end, stopping on the first red and resuming
tasks.description: Sketch section 0. Steps, each recorded in a resumable state file and skipped on resume once done: preflight (the open-bug and provisional-phase question guard-release asks, read from its own predicate, plus verify.sh --release's preflight); bump plugin.json; finalize the CHANGELOG section; the followers in verify.sh's #R order (README curl pins, examples/report.sh incl. docs/index.html, the scale demo commands check-rendered-artifacts --how prints, screenshots); tools/verify.sh --release; the release commit; push to a ci/<version> branch and gh workflow run ci.yml --ref it; wait for that run on that exact SHA (a cancelled run is not a failed one - read conclusion); annotated tag; push main and the tag; gh release create with the CHANGELOG section; check-release-published. The first red stops with the step, its excerpt and the resume command. Every remote step is named before it runs and nothing is pushed without an explicit --push the user typed (CLAUDE.md: permission to commit is not permission to push). guard-release learns to treat an invocation of tools/release.py as a publishing command so the #release-with-bugs bypass still governs it. The ci step is callable alone (release.py ci <ref>) so a landed phase can run CI the same way. A selftest drives every step against a fake runner, including resume after a stop at each step.

tasks.title: Doctor reports the git-snapshot setting and the README cost section names it
tasks.description: N4. A plugin cannot set includeGitInstructions or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS for its users (its settings carry only agent and subagentStatusLine), so this is a report and a documented recommendation. /audit:doctor reads the effective value (env var, then project .claude/settings.local.json and settings.json, then user settings) and names where it came from; it also reads, from the session's subagent transcripts, each later dispatch's first-request cache read and write so the user sees whether starts are served from cache. The README's cost section names the setting, recommends it at project level (a user-level setting removes Claude's built-in git instructions from every session), and states that the plugin's executors never commit and the driver commits by script. No figure is printed without the reading that produced it.

tasks.title: A phase boundary is a context boundary: a chained run starts each phase fresh and status shows the carried context
tasks.description: F630, measured on the testbed: P2-P10 ran back to back in one never-cleared orchestrator context, mean context per request grew from 136k to 589k, and the orchestrator's share of phase cost from about half to over three quarters - an estimated 18.7 of 33.66 USD-equivalent bought nothing, because everything a phase needs is on disk (manifest, journal, evidence, drive state, briefs). (1) When the drive prints `done` and the phase command continues to a next phase, the command body (commands/phase.md and the run/drive reference) directs a fresh context per phase: clear and re-enter with `/audit:phase <next>`, stated as the step, not a tip. (2) The drive's entry line and `/audit:status` read the orchestrator's current context size from the transcript the usage meter already scans, and past a stated threshold say what each further request costs at the dated price (the basis named, or 'unknown' when the transcript cannot be read - never a default). Micro-test: two trivial phases driven back to back as the command directs; the second phase's first orchestrator request carries no more context than a fresh entry within a stated margin (an offline fixture over recorded transcript rows, no paid call). Faults: F630.

tasks.title: The intent check grades the diff against the task text, and the drive checks tests.add against the filed tests
tasks.description: F633, measured on the testbed with a plain-session baseline and a blind A/B review: P5.3's text said src is set when the card ENTERS the viewport; the executor shipped `rootMargin: "200px 0px"`, said so, and renamed its test to 'once the card is near the viewport'; the phase reviewer's intentCheck answered `matches` on the basis of the executor's restatement. The blind pass also found two med defects the phase review missed. (1) The intent check QUOTES THE TASK TEXT and compares the diff and the tests against it - never against the outcome text or the test titles; a restatement whose scope differs from the task text is itself a finding, quoting both. (2) The reviewer brief puts the task text first and the executor's return last, labelled as the claim under review. (3) The drive diffs `tests.add` against the test names the return files, mechanically, and a declared case with no filed counterpart is a finding before any reviewer runs. Red-first: a fixture where the task says 'enters' and the return says 'near' with a 200px margin must answer `diverges` and quote both; a declared tests.add case missing from the return is named by the drive. (4) Measured on the testbed with the SAME model (plain Sonnet vs the plugin's Sonnet executors, blind A/B): the plugin's version alone shipped a lazy-load test that cannot fail, an e2e that drives the real server action (a key in env sends real mail), and a test-readiness race (asserting enabled state the SSR HTML already has). So the reviewer brief also asks, per declared test: can it fail on the unfixed code (the red-first block, or say it was never seen red), and does any test reach a real external service or side effect (mail, payment, network) rather than a stub - each a finding with its file:line. Faults: F633. (5) A FALSIFIER PER TEST, run by the drive at near-zero model cost (about +0.005 USD per task, research report 2026-10-12-agent-output-quality-research.md): every planned test carries a line 'must fail if <small code change>'; after the executor files, the drive applies that patch in a temporary tree (never the executor's tree) and runs the test, and a test that survives is a finding with file:line. A patch that breaks the build is could-not-run, never a kill. This REPLACES a revert-to-base check, which probe 1 measured as too weak: the plugin's P5.3 test fails on the revert yet survives the 'src set on mount' mutant, the real defect class; the plain Sonnet test kills both mount and margin_200 (artefacts danuvia-baseline/research-p53-plugin/probe-artifacts/probe1/*.log). (6) Parity in interaction states: when a task's design source names `:focus`/`:hover` rules for a form or control (as flux.css `.field input:focus` did), task synthesis writes into tests.add a design-parity case that snapshots that control's own box in its focus state (and hover where defined), not only rest, as a clipped element snapshot of that control or a computed-style assertion - a 1% threshold over a whole section hid a 2px ring (about 0.2% of the section) (2px/4px against the design's 9px, found by a live getComputedStyle probe). (7) Executor brief: scope must never push an executor into an inferior design. P6.3's plugin executor faked a 'Resend mock' by rewriting the browser response because `playwright.config.ts` was outside its scope; the plain session edited the config and ran a real mock. When the right design needs file X outside `files`, the executor files a widening request naming X and why, and does not work around it; P124's companions do not cover test infrastructure. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12, at the owner's request. (8) Probe 2 (24 reviewer runs, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, real P5.3 brief section): the brief as filed, task text first with the claim labelled, and the claim hidden each found 0/3 `diverges`; ONLY a CLAUSE-QUOTING RULE worked, 3/3 on all three models - the reviewer quotes each task clause, judges the diff against it, and a scope difference is `diverges`. So (1)-(2) are implemented as that rule, and: a contradicted clause carries a MED severity floor (4 of 6 Opus/Sonnet runs rated it low, which review-convergence would park as a carried low); the intent answer splits 'does the diff do what was asked' from 'does the claim describe the diff'; the phase brief carries tests.add, which it lacks today. (9) The tests.add-vs-filed-tests check of (3) cannot be a string diff: as one it flags 72 of 77 danuvia tasks, mostly Serbian plan text against English test titles. It matches a declared case by a verbatim title the executor must reuse, or by a clause mapping the return files; never a fuzzy string compare.

tasks.title: No report table can widen the page at any width, by construction rather than by font margin
tasks.description: Carried from P126-R2 (med, P126 phase review 2026-10-13). P126.1 made the hostile-content leg green on CI by letting the bugs table's test-gate pills wrap (`white-space:normal`), which lowers that column's narrowest width - so the page passes by margin at CI's fonts (reproduced with DejaVu in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.0-jammy: +31px before, 0 after), not by an invariant: any table whose columns' min-content widths sum past the column can still widen the document above the breakpoint where `.tablewrap` starts to scroll. The structural options trade against the sticky header: (a) `.tablewrap{overflow-x:auto}` at every width - a contained scroll that can never widen the document, but `position:sticky` on thead then sticks to the wrapper, not the viewport; (b) keep the viewport-sticky header and give every non-prose column a bounded min-width plus `<wbr>` in every renderer-emitted unbroken run; (c) a JS-measured fallback that switches a table to (a) only when it overflows. Decide with the owner, implement, and add a hostile-leg case that plants a token in EVERY column kind at the narrowest unframed width on a wide-font fixture so the margin cannot be what passes it. tasks.title: A concurrent writer that loses a Windows sharing race retries within its deadline instead of refusing the write
tasks.description: F615 recurred and has a twin, so this is the class, not two instances. CI run 38442950089 (ci/p125 at 125a69b8, windows-latest): test__journal_io sl4 lost a row to 'refused: [Errno 13] Permission denied ... .lock.break' (F615, first seen 2026-10-10, still unfixed), and test_panel_server hr2 had the second of two concurrent POST /api/proposal drops refused ([('first', True), ('second', False)]). Neither file changed since v3.3.0; both are intermittent (3.3.0's CI was green). The class: on Windows, opening, renaming or replacing a file another process holds is denied, and a writer that reads that denial as a refusal loses the write. One invariant in one place: the lock acquire / breaker / atomic-replace helpers (_locks, and the replace helper the writers share) treat a sharing denial as contention - retried with backoff within the operation's existing deadline - and only a deadline expiry is a refusal. Every concurrent writer (journal append, panel write, manifest write) goes through those helpers; no per-site retry loop. Simulate the denial in tests; never sleep for real beyond a few ms.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__locks.py: an acquire or replace that meets a simulated Windows sharing denial (PermissionError / EACCES on the lock, breaker or target file) retries within its deadline and succeeds once the holder lets go
plugins/audit/tests/test__journal_io.py: sl4's trial with a simulated denial on the .lock.break file writes every row (no refused append)
plugins/audit/tests/test_panel_server.py: two proposal drops posted at once both land when the second meets a simulated sharing denial

outcome.technical: Added _output.sharing_denied(exc) (OSError with errno EACCES; EPERM is not one) and _output.while_shared(op, deadline=None, clock=time.monotonic): retries a sharing denial every SHARING_PAUSE_SECONDS until the deadline (SHARING_WAIT_SECONDS=2.0 from now when none is given), raises any other error at once and raises the denial once the deadline passes. Routed through it: _locks (new _claim_shared wraps _claim inside acquire's existing deadline and in _take_over; _claim re-raises a sharing denial instead of answering error; a denial still there at the deadline becomes the error answer E_ERR; release's unlink, _take_over's unlink and _write_lock's os.replace), _journal_io (_acquire's O_EXCL create inside LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS on time.time, _release's unlink, the .lock.break predicate now _output.sharing_denied, write_merged's os.replace), _manifest_io.atomic_write_text's os.replace, and _panel_write.restore's os.replace. Tests: test__locks.py sd-block sd1-sd6 (claim denied twice then taken; release unlink denied twice then removed; denial past wait=0.2 refused at the deadline as E_ERR; ENOSPC tried once; atomic_write_text replace denied twice then lands; replace denied past a patched bound raises EACCES with the old file intact and no temp file); test__journal_io.py sl11-sl13 (_acquire create denied twice; _release unlink denied twice; sl4's race with each writer's first two creates of .lock and .lock.break denied, through a new optional deny argument to _RACE_WRITER/_race_trial); test_panel_server.py hr3 (two concurrent POST /api/proposal drops with the index lock's release unlink and claim each denied once both land); test__output.py ws1-ws5 (fake clock, sleep recorded rather than slept: retry then answer; non-EACCES raises at once with no pause; denial at deadline raises after exactly the allowed attempts; default bound; predicate readings). ws1-ws5 were written after the helper existed, so they were not seen red against HEAD. Results after the fix: test__locks 132/132, test__journal_io 262/262, test__output 264/264, test_panel_server 103/103, test__manifest_io 189/189; python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 6 exit 0, '334/334 files ok, 153 migrated to tests/, 16067 cases', no file red; ruff exit 0; vermin exit 0; tools/bench-hooks.py --gate exit 0 (3.12 and 3.13 within budget, 3.11 not measured, no interpreter here). Process note: the first _output.py Edit was refused by the plan gate before the scope was widened; a sed sent in the same batch had added two import lines, which I removed (empty diff) before stopping. A heredoc edit of _locks.py was refused by the plan gate after the widening; the same changes were made with the Edit tool. Follow-ups, not edited as instructed: usage/usage_ledger.py _replace_retrying is now redundant with atomic_write_text's retry; stamp-verification.py's throwaway-tree removal retry could use _output.while_shared.

tasks.title: A new session says once, without the network, when its model has no price or the last session's CLI cost disagrees with the plugin's, and is silent otherwise
tasks.description: Owner request, 2026-10-13: check model prices when a new orchestrator session starts, and prove it works, what it finds and what it costs. Design: no network (hooks are stdlib and fail-open, and no official per-token price API is known; a fetch stays an explicit command if ever). A SessionStart hook (a new mode of meter-usage.py rather than a new file, unless the measurement argues otherwise) checks (1) whether the session's model resolves in the price table (P125.2's rates_for; unpriced -> one line naming the model and the config remedy) and (2) whether the previous session's CLI cost-state (P125.4's read_cost_state / cli_cost_compare) diverges from the plugin's figure beyond CLI_COST_TOLERANCE_USD, printing both figures with their basis and the table's pricingAsOf. Silent when both pass: a quiet start costs zero context tokens. MEASUREMENT IS PART OF DONE, reported in the return with the commands that produce each number: (a) start latency of the new mode with tools/bench-hooks.py, against the hook budget (--gate must stay green); (b) bytes added to context when it fires, and that a quiet start adds none; (c) benefit: run the check (offline, read-only) over every recorded session transcript under <home>/.claude/projects for this repo and for the danuvia testbed, and report how many sessions it would fire on, split by cause (unpriced model / divergence), and for each divergence whether the cause is a stale price or something else (compaction trimming the transcript, subagent spend outside it). If divergence fires mostly for causes other than price, ship only check (1), keep (2) out, and say so with the numbers. Never write a measured number into README or code prose; the return carries it.

outcome.technical:
Added a SessionStart mode to the existing meter-usage.py hook (no new hook file): hooks.json now also wires meter-usage.py (open mode) on SessionStart. New function session_start_check(data, ul=None, cfg=None, root=None) finds the previous session's own transcript via a new usage_ledger.previous_session_transcript(data) helper (most-recently-modified sibling .jsonl beside the SessionStart payload's own transcript_path, excluded by session_id not by mtime/existence), reads that session's last assistant turn's model via the existing current_context_size, and checks usage_ledger.rates_for(model, table) - if the model has no price row, prints exactly one line naming the model and the usage.pricing remedy; otherwise silent. The message rides hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (not systemMessage), which is the one channel of this hook's output the model itself reads, routed in main() before meter() since a SessionStart payload's own transcript has no assistant turn yet to meter. Fails open (try/except returning None) on any missing/unreadable previous transcript, disabled config, or missing manifest.

A second check was implemented and then DROPPED before shipping, per the task's explicit measurement requirement: whether the previous session's CLI-reported cost-state (usage_ledger.read_cost_state, pre-existing from P125.4) disagrees with the ledger's own re-priced figure for that session (usage_ledger.cli_cost_divergences, also pre-existing), beyond CLI_COST_TOLERANCE_USD ($0.01). This was measured OFFLINE and READ-ONLY over every main-session transcript recorded under <home>/.claude/projects for this repo's own project directory and for the danuvia-software testbed project (neither transcript nor ledger directory was written to - only read.py/glob calls). Measurement commands (ad hoc, scratchpad-only, not committed): a short script loading usage_ledger.py by path, calling project_pricing(), current_context_size(), read_cost_state(), rates_for() and cli_cost_divergences() over every *.jsonl under each project's own <outside-repo><slug>/ directory, against each project's own real ledger (read via usage_ledger.read_ledger on the ledgerDir each project's own .claude/audit.config.json names).

Numbers (every one reproducible by re-running the commands named beside it):
- (a) start latency, `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py` after adding a 'sessionstart' LANES entry for meter-usage.py (the quiet/no-previous-session path, the common case): meter-usage.py/sessionstart measured at 50.49ms median of 9 (ratio 2.64x a bare interpreter start of 19.22ms) on this run - in the same range as the other 9 existing hook lanes (36-55ms, ratio 1.90x-2.87x on this run); this is NOT a gate per bench-hooks.py's own design (wall clock swings between repeats). `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` (the actual gate, the import-weight budget) stays green: exit 0, '10 hook(s) within budget' on all 6 interpreters found on this machine (3.8.20, 3.9.24, 3.10.19, 3.12.12, 3.13.12, 3.14.7) - meter-usage.py's module-level imports are unchanged, since the new code is a branch inside the same already-counted file.
- (b) bytes added to context: piping a real SessionStart JSON payload into `python3 plugins/audit/hooks/meter-usage.py` and measuring stdout with `wc -c`: a quiet start (previous session's model priced, or no previous session at all) writes 0 bytes to stdout; a firing start (previous session's model unpriced) writes 334 bytes, all of it the hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext JSON carrying one sentence.
- (c) offline benefit, read-only over recorded transcripts: this repo's own project directory held 13 main-session transcripts, the danuvia-software testbed held 18 (31 total). The SHIPPED check (unpriced model) would have fired on 2 of the 31 (one per project) - both were sessions whose last assistant turn named model '<synthetic>' (a test/eval artifact, not a real model the price table was ever expected to carry), silent on the other 29. The DROPPED check (cost-state divergence) was also measured on the same 31 transcripts against each project's real ledger: divergent (model, session) pairs existed in both projects; grouping them by model and looking at the CLI/plugin cost RATIO across every session that model diverged in - the test a single static mispriced rate would have to pass (a constant ratio) - only one model (2 sessions, in danuvia-software) held a near-constant ratio; every other model measured (7 distinct models across both projects, session counts of 1-11) scattered across a wide range session to session, and a meaningful share of the divergent pairs had no ledger row recorded for that session/model at all (metering gap, not a priced disagreement). tasks.title: A usage-ledger month rewrite never waits on its own open handle: it lets go of the tail before the replace, and the shared sharing-denial retry is its only retry
tasks.description: Regression introduced in this phase, caught by CI run 38517006899 (ci/p125 at a7d1b5c4, windows-latest plain and cp1252): test_audit_usage bw14 'a row appended while a refused replace is retried survives the replace' got calls=66/70 instead of 2 (count=1, code=0). P125.38 made _manifest_io.atomic_write_text retry a sharing denial (_output.while_shared, up to SHARING_WAIT_SECONDS); usage_ledger's month rewrite keeps its OWN tail handle open while it calls _replace_rows, so on Windows the first replace now spins ~2 s against itself before raising, and only then does the old except-branch drain and close the tail and call _replace_retrying. Structural fix: drain and close the rewrite's own tail handle before the replace (the lock already excludes appenders), so the only holder a retry can meet is someone else, and delete _replace_retrying (the shared helper is the one retry). Keep bw14's guarantee: an append between the last read and the swap waits for the swap and survives. Net code down.

tasks.title: A follower a gate step owes is a record with a recipe, and the drive regenerates a generated follower in the task's own commit
tasks.description: Phase-review finding (med, CLASS - recurred on two P125 tasks): any task that adds an import regenerates PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's module map outside its files, so every such task ends in an undeclared-change decision. tasks.title: The drive speaks in one-line signals, a brief per task and an explain on demand; phase.md and orchestrator.md are rewritten to the seven verbs
tasks.description: Phase-review finding (med, CLASS - recurred on three P125 tasks): commands/phase.md sits at its byte ceiling in tools/measure-context.py, so every flag added to the run form trims unrelated prose, and the trims hit sentences other gates pin. Implement consolidated plan F2.5 (approved 2026-10-14), which rewrites P128.5. `drive-phase.py next --signal` prints one line of at most 200 bytes in the form `audit <phase> <verb> <subject> [auto...] | <basis> | next: <one command or wait>`, with the verbs dispatch, wait, ask, judge, review, done and stop. `brief <id>` prints the executor brief with the stable text first and the task-specific part last. `--explain <id>` gives at most 2 KB. The dispatch prompt is one fixed sentence plus the id, so two dispatch prompts are identical up to the id. Rewrite reference/orchestrator.md and commands/phase.md to the seven verbs, and LOWER measure-context's ceilings for them. The multi-line `decide-*` prompts in STEPS stop being the main channel and stay only behind --explain. Prefer removals (owner decision D9).

tasks.title: A task's start is identified uniquely, so a restart within the same second never reads the previous start's return or marks
tasks.description: Seen on CI run 38575164197 (ubuntu spaced leg, test_drive_phase sc4): after `--answer retry` the attempts went 1 -> 2, yet the next step printed the OLD start's scope-changed decision ('filed under 1 files'), because the return path and the drive's per-start marks are keyed by `startedAt` at one-second resolution (`_filed_returns.return_start_key`, `drive-phase.start_key`): a restart inside the same second as the start it replaces gets the same key, so it finds the previous start's filed return, its `gated` mark and its brief. A fast runner does this; locally sc4 passed twelve times out of twelve. Invariant: every start has an identity no earlier start of the task can share (the attempt number in the key, or a strictly increasing stamp - one definition, read by every place that keys by start: return paths, drive marks, briefs, attempts records), with returns already filed under the old key still found. Make sc4 deterministic: pin the clock so the restart lands in the start's second, and prove it red against today's key.

New `_filed_returns.next_start_at(previous, now)` (with START_AT_FORMAT and `_start_epoch`, stdlib calendar/time): a `now` at or before the task's previous `startedAt` becomes the second after it; a later second is kept as read; an unparseable previous bounds nothing. `audit-task.py _start_task` now stamps `startedAt = _fr.next_start_at(was['startedAt'], now)`; its docstrings and `_start_changes`' docstring and the `_filed_returns` module docstring updated to name the mechanism. Resolution asked: Run commit before verify-release (or run the --before-commit half before the commit and the full --release after it), and add a case whose fake verify.sh answer depends on whether a commit was recorded.

P125-R22: wait_ci resolves the pushed branch with `git rev-parse ci/v<version>`, but step_push_ci_branch pushes `HEAD:refs/heads/ci/v<version>` and creates no local branch; only refs/remotes/origin/ci/v<version> exists. Checked in a scratch repo: after that push `git rev-parse ci/v1.2.3` exits 128 ('unknown revision') while `git rev-parse origin/ci/v1.2.3` resolves. So with --push the wait-ci step always stops 'could not resolve ci/v... to a commit'. rl3/rl4/rl5 stub `git rev-parse ci/v9.9.9` to succeed, so no case can fail on this.

Resolution asked: Resolve the SHA from HEAD at push time (store it in state with ciBranch) or use `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`/`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>`, and make the fake runner answer rev-parse of a bare ci/ ref with failure.

P125-R23: A run without --push records push-ci-branch, wait-ci, push-main-tag, gh-release and check-published as status 'done' ('skipped: no --push given'), and run_pipeline skips any step already done. A later `release.py run --version X --push` therefore finds every remote step done, publishes nothing and prints 'RELEASE vX COMPLETE'; the local tag step has already run too. rl2b asserts exactly this recording as intended. The documented dry-run-then-push use ends in a false success.

Resolution asked: Record a skipped remote step as 'skipped' (not 'done') and treat it as pending when --push is given, or refuse a --push resume over a state file whose remote steps were skipped; add a case that runs without --push and then with it and expects the push.

P125-R25: Clause 'including resume after a stop at each step' is met only for the CI step (rl3/rl4). No case stops at bump, changelog, followers, verify-release, commit, push, tag, push-main-tag or gh-release and resumes, which is how findings 1 to 3 survived a green selftest.

Resolution asked: Drive a table of steps, failing each in turn with the fake runner and resuming, asserting the earlier steps do not re-run and the failed one does.

P125-R98: The task says 'rl8, and any case asserting on the fake runner's call list, prints the whole call list on failure ... Clip the message'. Only rl8 was clipped. rl2 still formats '%r' % (runner.calls,) unclipped (also the only other call-list print at :751-756). It is bounded by the new call_limit=200 but not clipped. The clause is contradicted for rl2.

Resolution asked: Route rl2's message through excerpt(repr(runner.calls)) like rl8 and rl8b. Optionally add a helper that every call-list message uses.

(1) STEPS reordered so commit precedes verify-release; docstring says why (verify.sh --release's --against-commit arm is red while a re-render is uncommitted) and that a red verify leaves only a local commit to amend. (2) step_push_ci_branch reads `git rev-parse HEAD` before `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/ci/v<v>` and records ciSha in the state; wait_ci(ctx, ref, sha=None) takes the known sha and resolves ref locally only when none is given (kept for `ci <ref>`); step_wait_ci uses state ciSha, falling back to `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`, never the bare ci/ name. (3) The no --push skip moved out of five step functions into run_pipeline: a remote step is recorded status 'skipped' (step_done does not count it), so a later --push run over the same state runs it; a run that skipped any remote step ends with 'release vX prepared locally and nothing was published: ... skipped' plus a publish command instead of COMPLETE. (4) FakeRunner results may be callables; new _new_world()/_faithful_responses(): bare `git rev-parse ci/...` fails 128, origin/ci/... resolves only after the push, `git rev-parse HEAD` returns the head, verify.sh --release is red until `git commit` was recorded, gh run list reports the pushed sha. rl3/rl4 moved onto it (they previously stubbed the bare ci ref to succeed). tasks.title: the machine-path shapes: writer keeps relative repo paths, detector catches cut
tasks.description:
Phase-review findings fixed together (one theme, shared files).

P125-R53: P125.27 makes the write scrub stricter. Before, `posix-home` fired at the writer only with a separator before the home word, and the removed comment justified that: a repository may hold its own `home/` directory and a writer refusing `home/<x>` would refuse its paths. Now a relative repo path with no leading separator such as `<outside-repo>` (home word plus two further segments, depth 3) fires. P125-R91: `fit_clauses` does `keep.pop()` over the clauses `did_events` reads (closed/started/landed/fix-added/signed/released) when they exceed the byte room. A wave member's tree holds a committed copy of the manifest, and `submit_command` spells the manifest absolutely and adds `--project-dir` for exactly that reason. The tests call `M.main(["brief", subject, mpath, "--role", role, "--project-dir", root])`, so they never run the command the agent is actually given.
